Q: What is the difference between the 'COPY' and 'ADD' commands in a Dockerfile? A:

  1. ADD deepak.tar.gz

    The above example is the add operation in the docker file. It has similar functionality of copy but this is mainly used whenever we want to copy something from a remote URL, Or we want to untar/unzip a file during the container creation. Also ADD will create less layers as compare to copy thereby decreasing the size of your image.

  2. COPY deepak.tar.gz

    The above example is used when we want to copy files or directories from the host machine. Copy tends to create extra layers within the docker image.

Q: Extract each year, month, day, year from getctime and getmtime in Python A:

The time.ctime function returns the local time in string form. You might want to use the time.localtime function, which returns a struct_time object which contains the information you are looking for. As example,

import os, time

date_created_string = time.ctime(os.path.getctime('/home/b-fg/Downloads'))
date_created_obj = time.localtime(os.path.getctime('/home/b-fg/Downloads'))
print(date_created_string) # Mon Feb 10 09:41:03 2020
print('Year: {:4d}'.format(date_created_obj.tm_year)) # Year: 2020
print('Month: {:2d}'.format(date_created_obj.tm_mon)) # Month:  2
print('Day: {:2d}'.format(date_created_obj.tm_mday)) # Day: 10

Note that these are integer values, as requested.

Q: Accessing Swift function in a framework from Objective-C AppDelegate.m A:

In my experience using @import ModuleName; usually brings in the @objc elements into ObjC code. You can also mark regular functions @objc and call them as functions, not classes.
